references.text: Carrying poles of acacia wood were also made for the ark of the covenant, and they were overlaid with gold. This shows the same pattern for making carrying poles for holy objects.
Carrying poles of acacia wood were made for the table of showbread, demonstrating the same construction method for the tabernacle's furnishings.
The context for the altar of burnt offering, for which the carrying poles were to be used, includes that the altar itself was overlaid with bronze.
The altar of incense also had carrying poles of acacia wood, showing the same design standard for all altars in the tabernacle.
The fulfillment of this commandment, where the carrying poles were made of acacia wood and overlaid with bronze for the altar of burnt offering.
The carrying poles were used by the Levites to carry the altar when the Israelites broke camp and traveled through the wilderness.
The contrast between the altar's bronze (judgment/sacrifice) and the sanctuary's gold (divinity) illustrates two sides of the plan of salvation.
It is the historical fulfillment of the instruction in the source verse, confirming that the poles were made exactly as God commanded.
Confirms the execution of the showbread table's poles and highlights the contrast with the bronze poles of the altar of sacrifice.
Confirms the execution of the incense altar's poles and illuminates the contrast between the inner (gold) and outer (bronze) altars.
